ai.description: Minervarya kadar is a small frog (SVL 25–30 mm) with a brown, mottled dorsum and pale belly. It is distinguished by a prominent, shovel-shaped inner metatarsal tubercle and distinct toe webbing.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya kadar* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and prominent glandular fold running along the dorsolateral side of its body.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya kadar* inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at mid-to-high altitudes between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kadar burrowing frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its underground retreats during the monsoon season to forage for small invertebrates on the forest floor.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya kadar* is an oviparous species that breeds during the monsoon season, laying clutches of approximately 100–200 eggs in small, temporary rain pools.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya kadar* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically inhabiting the Anamalai and Nilgiri hills in Kerala and Tamil Nadu at mid-to-high elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Kadar Burrowing Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched, metallic chirps. These rhythmic calls are typically heard from water-filled depressions in forest habitats.
